about: A cheat sheet of Ollama commands. Each row says where it comes from: Ollama's own documentation, or a third-party guide where the official pages do not cover it.

glukhov.title: Ollama CLI Cheatsheet (glukhov.org, says it was checked against Ollama v0.33.2)

centron.title: Managing Ollama models: updates and cleanup (centron.de)

items.what: Download a model without starting a chat. Use the exact tag from this page (for example gpt-oss:20b).
Chat with a model in the terminal.
items.note: Add --verbose to print speed after each answer (see Check and troubleshoot below).

items.what: Opens a setup menu that configures other tools (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, Droid) to use your Ollama models. For example, ollama launch claude.
List the models downloaded to this computer, with sizes.
items.note: The sizes can add up to more than the real disk use, because models share files (see the disk-use row under Check and troubleshoot).

items.what: List the models loaded in memory right now. The Processor column shows where each one runs: 100% GPU, 100% CPU, or a split such as 71%/29% CPU/GPU.
Details about a downloaded model: size, context length, quantization. Flags such as --modelfile, --parameters and --license narrow the output.
items.note: Not on Ollama's own CLI page; run ollama show --help to confirm on your version.

groups.title: Remove a model or free memory

items.what: Unload a model from memory now. By default Ollama keeps a model loaded for 5 minutes after the last use.
Delete a downloaded model from disk. You can name several, separated by spaces.
items.note: Check ollama ps first: deleting a model that is loaded can leave a running request in an undefined state. If two tags share the same ID, remove both to free the space.

items.what: Copy a model under a new name without downloading it again. Useful before you edit a Modelfile.
Ollama downloads updates by itself. Click the Ollama icon in the taskbar or menu bar and choose Restart to update. You can also install the latest version over the top.
Linux: update Ollama by running the install script again.
Update a model you already have: pull it again. One guide says Ollama then downloads only the files that changed, and finishes quickly if nothing changed.
items.note: That guide gives no single command to update every model at once. A tag such as 8b can be republished with different weights, so pull the exact tag you use.

items.what: Make a customized model from a Modelfile (this page uses it to raise the context length).
The default context window is 4096 tokens. This environment variable raises it (this exact example is from Ollama's FAQ). A bigger context uses more memory.
How long a model stays in memory after use. The default is 5 minutes. Setting it when the server starts changes it for all models.
Let other computers on your network use this Ollama. By default it only listens on this computer.

Move where models are stored. Default folders: Windows C:\Users\<you>\.ollama\models, macOS ~/.ollama/models, Linux /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models. On Linux the ollama user needs read and write access to the new folder.
Lists the environment variables the server understands.

groups.title: How to set an environment variable

items.what: Quit Ollama from the tray icon, edit the variable for your user account, then start Ollama again.
Run launchctl setenv with the variable and its value, then restart the Ollama app.
Add the variable under [Service], then run systemctl daemon-reload and systemctl restart ollama.
Prints timing after each answer. The eval rate line is the speed in tokens per second. Ask twice and use the second answer: the first one after loading is slower.
items.note: The second-run advice is from this page's own measurements (see calibration.md), not from the guide.

items.what: Windows: opens the folder with server.log (newest) and server-#.log (older).
macOS: show the server log.
Linux (systemd): follow the server log. If you started ollama serve in a terminal, the log is in that terminal.
Real disk use of your models (Linux service installs: sudo du -sh /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models). Ollama has no prune command, so interrupted downloads can leave unused files behind.
Sign in to or out of your Ollama account.
